main.title: Guacamelee!
main.subtitle: Lucha libre between the worlds of the living and the dead
main.summary: Guacamelee! is a Metroidvania action platforming video game developed and published by DrinkBox Studios.

cards.heading: Guacamelee! debuts on PS3 and PS Vita
cards.text: Guacamelee! is a Metroidvania action platforming video game developed and published by DrinkBox Studios, initially launched in April 2013 for platforms PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita and was later ported to Windows in August and to OS X and Linux in February 2014. The enhanced Super Turbo Championship Edition was released for Wii U, Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Xbox 360 in July 2014 and later on the Nintendo Switch in October 2018. The game is inspired by traditional Mexican culture and folklore, like alebrijes and Day of the Dead.

cards.heading: Juan, Tostada and cooperative combat
cards.text: Guacamelee! is a hybrid 2D Metroidvania-style action platform and brawler. Players control the luchador Juan and explore an open, non-linear world to complete the central story objectives while collecting necessary character upgrades and battling enemies. Coins collected from defeated enemies are used to buy new skills at shops, which also double as checkpoints. The game features drop-in co-op play, with the second player assuming the role of Tostada, Guardian of the Mask.

cards.heading: New moves open new paths
cards.text: As players progress through the game, Juan breaks open "Choozo statues", a direct reference to Metroid's "Chozo statues", to gain new abilities. Some abilities give Juan new combat options with each move's color corresponding to similarly colored obstacles in the world, requiring Juan to learn specific moves before accessing certain areas. Other abilities include movement upgrades, such as a double jump, a chicken transformation to traverse small corridors, and the ability to cross between the world of the living and the world of the dead to access areas and combat enemies that reside in one plane.

main.title: Tomodachi Life
main.subtitle: Nintendo SPD · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Tomodachi Life is Nintendo's Nintendo 3DS social simulation about an island of Mii characters. The player creates or imports its residents, adjusts their voices and personalities, then watches them establish friendships, arguments and romances. A cast can resemble friends, relatives, celebrities or a deliberately unlikely mixture of all three. The island's daily life gives those familiar faces unpredictable combinations. Instead of assigning a fixed role to each resident, the player attends to requests and discovers what the group does when left to develop relationships of its own.

cards.heading: An island populated by familiar faces
cards.text: Tomodachi Life is Nintendo's Nintendo 3DS social simulation about an island of Mii characters. The player creates or imports its residents, adjusts their voices and personalities, then watches them establish friendships, arguments and romances. A cast can resemble friends, relatives, celebrities or a deliberately unlikely mixture of all three. The island's daily life gives those familiar faces unpredictable combinations. Instead of assigning a fixed role to each resident, the player attends to requests and discovers what the group does when left to develop relationships of its own.

cards.heading: Help with the small problem in an apartment
cards.text: A Mii might want food, different clothes, company or help resolving a disagreement. Meeting that request changes the resident's mood and can open another interaction. Personality and relationships supply context, so the same item may be received differently by another person. The player's influence stays close to those immediate needs. The pleasure often comes from the gap between the person represented and the situation the game invents, with text-to-speech voices making an unexpected remark sound as though it belongs to that particular resident.

cards.heading: Give the cast a stage
cards.text: Shops, public places and performances draw the Miis outside their apartments. Songs can be arranged with customised lyrics, turning the resident cast into performers for a miniature show. Dreams and other scenes provide further glimpses of their peculiar lives. The overseas release followed in 2014 after extensive work on localisation and speech, adapting details for different audiences. Tomodachi Life turns character creation into an ongoing source of comedy: a face takes only a little time to make, but the island keeps finding another situation in which to place it.

main.title: Don't Starve
main.subtitle: Wilson must survive in the Constant
main.summary: Don't Starve is a survival game developed and published by Klei Entertainment.

cards.heading: The computer launch and later editions
cards.text: Don?t Starve is a survival game developed and published by Klei Entertainment. It first launched for Windows, OS X and Linux on April 23, 2013. The Reign of Giants expansion followed in 2014, and the separate multiplayer game Don?t Starve Together let players face its dangers together.

cards.heading: Hunger, health and sanity in the Constant
cards.text: The game follows a scientist named Wilson who finds himself in a dark, dreary parallel world known as the Constant and must survive as long as possible. To this end, the player must keep Wilson alive, fed, and mentally stable as he avoids a variety of surreal and supernatural enemies that will try to kill and devour him. The game's Adventure mode adds depth to the sparse plot and pits Wilson against the game's supposed antagonist, Maxwell.

main.title: Metro: Last Light
main.subtitle: Artyom between Moscow’s tunnels and the contaminated surface
main.summary: Metro: Last Light is a 2013 first-person shooter video game developed by 4A Games and published by Deep Silver.

cards.heading: Artyom searches for the Dark Ones
cards.text: Metro: Last Light is a 2013 first-person shooter video game developed by 4A Games and published by Deep Silver. A sequel to the video game Metro 2033 and the second installment in the Metro series, its story follows Artyom, a young soldier living in the Moscow Metro after a devastating nuclear war. Tasked with finding the mysterious Dark Ones, Artyom must venture to different parts of the metro system, and the surface filled with radiated gases, and fight against different factions and mutated monsters. The game improves on various gameplay mechanics of 2033, and introduces elements such as weapon customization.

cards.heading: Exploration, ammunition and supplies
cards.text: Artyom moves through Moscow's tunnels and occasional journeys above ground, fighting hostile people and mutants. Larger areas offer several routes, making quiet movement and exploration alternatives to a direct firefight. Supplies remain scarce. Military-grade ammunition serves as money at stations, so firing it spends something that could buy a weapon or attachment later. Lower-quality rounds preserve that currency but offer another compromise. Searching bodies and rooms for ammunition therefore supports both survival and future purchases. Scopes, silencers and the choice of route let the player decide how to use those limited resources.

cards.heading: Glukhovsky and the making of the sequel
cards.text: Developed by a team of about 80 people, Last Light is a direct sequel to 2033, with franchise creator Dmitry Glukhovsky writing the game's dialogue and main story outline. Multiplayer modes were planned but were eventually scrapped in order to focus on single-player, which the developers hoped would "rekindle memories of Half-Life 2". The game was originally set to be published by THQ, which provided a very limited budget for the game's development, causing the team to work under extremely difficult conditions. Koch Media acquired the rights to the franchise following THQ's bankruptcy. A planned Wii U version was ultimately canceled. The game was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in May 2013.

main.title: Shin Megami Tensei IV
main.subtitle: Atlus · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Shin Megami Tensei IV is Atlus's Nintendo 3DS role-playing game about Flynn, a new samurai of the Eastern Kingdom of Mikado. His duties take him below the kingdom into a devastated Tokyo inhabited by demons and competing human factions. The journey moves between places whose beliefs give different answers to how people should live. Flynn's companions help expose those divisions, while the player assembles a changing party of demons. The story's choices develop alongside a battle system in which understanding the opposition can decide an encounter remarkably quickly.

cards.heading: A samurai discovers another city
cards.text: Shin Megami Tensei IV is Atlus's Nintendo 3DS role-playing game about Flynn, a new samurai of the Eastern Kingdom of Mikado. His duties take him below the kingdom into a devastated Tokyo inhabited by demons and competing human factions. The journey moves between places whose beliefs give different answers to how people should live. Flynn's companions help expose those divisions, while the player assembles a changing party of demons. The story's choices develop alongside a battle system in which understanding the opposition can decide an encounter remarkably quickly.

cards.heading: An enemy can become an ally
cards.text: Talking to a demon opens a negotiation instead of another exchange of attacks. It may demand money, items or a particular answer before agreeing to join. Recruited demons bring different resistances and skills, then supply material for fusion into another form. Choosing which abilities the new demon inherits lets the party change without discarding everything learned along the way. Flynn can also acquire skills from his companions. The collection is a set of possible roles, with each new recruit offering another answer to a dangerous matchup.

cards.heading: Make an opening count
cards.text: The Press Turn system rewards exploiting weaknesses and landing critical hits with additional actions. A blocked or absorbed attack can waste opportunities instead. These rules apply to both sides, so an enemy can turn one exposed resistance into a damaging sequence. Preparation involves inspecting the party's weaknesses as carefully as its strongest attacks. Flynn explores three-dimensional streets and interiors between these battles, taking requests that reveal more of Tokyo. The city supplies the people and factions whose conflicting hopes give his growing strength a direction.

main.title: The Swapper
main.subtitle: Clones and consciousness aboard an abandoned station
main.summary: The Swapper is a 2013 puzzle-platform game.

cards.heading: Transferring consciousness to solve puzzles
cards.text: The Swapper is a 2013 puzzle-platform game. A science fiction-themed title, the player controls a scavenger stranded aboard an abandoned research station, and discovers the strange titular device, which allows her to create clones of herself and switch her consciousness between these clones. The player uses this ability to solve various puzzles and learn about the fate of the station's researchers. The game's plot explores philosophical themes including the nature of consciousness, identity, telepathy, and the mind–body problem, with two of its main characters named after famous philosophers Daniel Dennett and David Chalmers.

cards.heading: Development in Helsinki and critical reception
cards.text: The Swapper was developed by Facepalm Games, an independent developer in Helsinki, Finland, and released on May 30, 2013, for Microsoft Windows, Mac OS X, and Linux. It was ported to PlayStation and Nintendo by Curve Studios in 2014. The game was released to critical acclaim, with reviewers praising the game's visual style and atmosphere, puzzle quality, and innovative mechanics.

main.title: Remember Me
main.subtitle: Nilin and the memories of Neo-Paris
main.summary: Remember Me is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by Dontnod Entertainment and published by Capcom.

cards.heading: Nilin confronts the Memorize corporation
cards.text: Remember Me is a 2013 action adventure developed by Dontnod Entertainment and published by Capcom. Nilin, a memory hunter in Neo-Paris, begins the game stripped of most of her own memories by the Memorize corporation. With help from the mysterious Edge and the underground Errorists, she seeks to recover her past and bring down the company. Her Memory Remix ability lets her alter another person's recollection of an event.

cards.heading: Remixing and stealing memories
cards.text: Remember Me features platforming, exploration and melee combat. The game is played as Nilin from a third-person view and introduces the mechanic of memory remixing: entering and rearranging a target's memories to manipulate them. Players accomplish this by replaying a memory and modifying details to change the target's recollection of the outcome. Another key mechanic of the gameplay is stealing memories from certain targets and using points called Remembranes to replay the memory in real-time: this is often needed to proceed through the game or avoid hazards otherwise hidden from the player. When the player is low on health, the screen will glitch until a sufficient amount of health is regained. On occasion, Nilin encounters puzzles in the form of riddles she must solve to unlock doors so as to further progress in the story.

cards.heading: Dontnod’s debut, from Adrift to Remember Me
cards.text:
Remember Me was developed as the debut project of Dontnod Entertainment, with one of the company's founding members Jean-Maxime Moris as its director. Part of his goal for the game was to create a thought-provoking narrative, and eventually settled on a female protagonist to help convey the story's themes. Originally a PlayStation 3 exclusive under Sony Computer Entertainment titled Adrift, it was cancelled in 2011 and later purchased by Capcom which resurrected it as a multi-platform game.

Remember Me was released for the PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360 in June 2013. The game received mixed reviews from critics upon release; praise was given to its world design, Olivier Deriviere's soundtrack, the ambition of the story and the Memory Remix segments, while the main criticisms laid against other aspects of the story, poor design choices and formulaic combat. It sold over 1 million units by 2016.

main.title: The Last of Us
main.subtitle: Joel and Ellie cross a post-pandemic America
main.summary: The Last of Us follows Joel and Ellie across a post-pandemic United States, combining stealth, combat and the search for scarce supplies.

cards.heading: Testing an encounter between shelves
cards.text: The Last of Us follows Joel as he escorts Ellie across a post-pandemic United States. Stealth and combat take place in abandoned buildings, towns and overgrown landscapes. Programmer Christian Gyrling recalls an early drugstore prototype in which enemies moved around bookshelves while the player slipped between them. Designer Matthew Gallant tested such encounters with colleagues outside the design department to see how unfamiliar players approached them.

cards.heading: Acting before the animation
cards.text: Gallant recalls developers acting out movements in the office to show colleagues what they needed from an animation. Cinematic animator Eric Baldwin describes the original game?s facial performances being key-framed, with close attention to subtle expressions. Gesture, timing and animation helped carry the characters? emotions into the finished scenes.

cards.heading: Beauty beside the damage
cards.text: Naughty Dog described contrast as a guiding idea for its environments: beauty would remain visible amid the destruction. Quiet stretches allow Joel and Ellie to talk and observe their surroundings between dangerous encounters. The studio worked with Area5 on a film documenting how these places were made.

cards.heading: Crossing a post-pandemic America
cards.text: The Last of Us is an action-adventure game played from a third-person perspective. The player traverses post-apocalyptic environments such as towns, buildings, forests, and sewers to advance the story. The player can use firearms, improvised weapons, hand-to-hand combat, and stealth to defend against hostile humans and cannibalistic creatures infected by a mutated strain of the Cordyceps fungus. For most of the game, the player takes control of Joel, a man tasked with escorting a young girl, Ellie, across the United States. The player also controls Ellie throughout the game's winter segment and briefly controls Joel's daughter, Sarah, in the opening sequence.

cards.heading: Scavenging weapons and crafting supplies
cards.text: In combat, the player can use long-range weapons, such as a rifle, a shotgun, and a bow, and short-range weapons such as a handgun and a short-barreled shotgun. The player is able to scavenge limited-use melee weapons, such as pipes and baseball bats, and throw bottles and bricks to distract, stun, or attack enemies. The player can upgrade weapons at workbenches using collected items. Equipment such as health kits, shivs, and Molotov cocktails can be found or crafted using collected items. Attributes such as the health meter and crafting speed can be upgraded by collecting pills and medicinal plants. Health can be recharged by finding edible items or through the use of health kits.

cards.heading: Listen Mode, cover and exploration
cards.text: Though the player can attack enemies directly, they can also use stealth to attack undetected or sneak by them. "Listen Mode" allows the player to locate enemies through a heightened sense of hearing and spatial awareness, indicated as outlines visible through walls and objects. In the dynamic cover system, the player can crouch behind obstacles to gain a tactical advantage during combat. The game features periods without combat, often involving conversation between the characters. The player can solve simple puzzles, such as using floating pallets to move Ellie, who is unable to swim, across bodies of water and using ladders or dumpsters to reach higher areas. Story collectibles, such as notes, maps and comics, can be scavenged and viewed in the backpack menu.

cards.heading: Enemies and companions react to combat
cards.text: The game features an artificial intelligence system by which hostile human enemies react to combat. If enemies discover the player, they may take cover or call for assistance and can take advantage of the player being distracted, out of ammunition, or in a fight. Player companions, such as Ellie, can assist in combat by throwing objects at threats to stun them, announcing the location of unseen enemies, or using a knife and pistol to attack enemies.

main.title: Company of Heroes 2
main.subtitle: Eastern Front strategy, visibility and winter conditions
main.summary: Company of Heroes 2 is a real-time strategy video game developed by Relic Entertainment and published by Sega for Windows, Linux, and OS X.

cards.heading: The Second World War on the Eastern Front
cards.text:
Company of Heroes 2 is a real-time strategy video game developed by Relic Entertainment and published by Sega for Windows, Linux, and OS X. It is the sequel to the 2006 game Company of Heroes. As with the original Company of Heroes, the game is set in World War II but with the focus on the Eastern Front, with players primarily controlling the side of the Soviet Red Army during various stages of the Eastern Front, from Operation Barbarossa to the Battle of Berlin. Company of Heroes 2 runs on Relic Entertainment's proprietary Essence 3.0 game engine.

In January 2013, Sega acquired Relic Entertainment and along with it the Company of Heroes intellectual property from THQ. The game was released on June 25 in North America and Europe.

cards.heading: TrueSight and unit visibility
cards.text: The game's Essence 3.0 engine introduces a new line-of-sight feature called the TrueSight system, which aims to better emulate troop visibility in real combat. In contrast to overhead visibility seen in other strategy games, TrueSight more accurately represents a unit's visibility range based on environmental conditions and type of unit.

cards.heading: ColdTech: snow, shelter and ice
cards.text: Winter conditions affect movement and survival. Soldiers exposed to severe cold lose body heat, shown by a thermometer beside their unit icon; fires and buildings provide shelter. Deep snow slows movement and leaves tracks that opponents can follow. Frozen rivers open alternative routes, but explosions can shatter the ice beneath advancing troops.
